task_1.valid_sector: rho_0<1/2, where a positive attained discrete maximum exists
task_1.global_issue: For rho_0>1/2 every finite-mode contribution is negative and tends to 0 from below; the displayed max does not exist. A nonnegative critical temperature uses sup=0 (or has infimum 0 if T is required strictly positive).

proof_carrying_search.reason: D(q) is concave and q decreases with shell m; the guaranteed representable axis shell ceil(sqrt(m_cont))^2 brackets the optimum.

task_2.reason: Literal execution of the displayed frozen formula gives shell 34 and Tc=0.0944939203368691; the frozen code block and reported output are mutually inconsistent.

task_3.reason: Solving q_vertex<1 gives 2+4alpha. At alpha=0.6, rho=0.37 the correct criterion predicts the finite mode found in Task 2, while the frozen criterion predicts no finite mode.

task_4.reason: The PRL supplement and direct residue algebra give rho_m=(1+alpha)/(2+4alpha); the exponent xi=(1+5alpha)/(2+4alpha) is valid.

task_5.reason: Expanding T-D(k) produces a minus sign in A4. Maximizing the conserved growth -A2 s^2-A4 s^3 gives s=-2A2/(3A4); the frozen solution derives this stationary point and then prints a different answer.

verdict.a100_reason: All decisive checks are closed-form or a 36-shell finite enumeration; GPU execution would add no evidential value.
